cards.source_title: Petroglyph — official solution
cards.scope_read: Complete short solution text; described diagram, not an independent reconstruction.
cards.observed: The explanation associates black segments with gray circles and curved arrows.
cards.representation_shift: Circles locate rotation centers; arrows prescribe how segments move.

suggested_test.description: Apply one direction convention to several unused groups; reject it if their transformed endpoints fail to align.

cards.transfer_when: Repeated marks could define a common geometric operation, as when centers and arcs accompany separate segments.
cards.dont_transfer_when: There is no stable pivot or direction convention, or alignment requires a different adjustment for each group.
cards.outcome_limit: A published transformation is supplied; the source does not report an unspoiled solver discovery.
cards.lesson: Ask what a mark operates on before treating it as another object to identify.

cards.source_title: Word Search II — official solution and author notes
cards.scope_read: Complete solution text and author notes.
cards.observed: A practice round reveals the targets while guesses receive two distance values.
cards.representation_shift: Separate vowel and consonant sequences; each output combines edit-distance contributions from different targets.
cards.documented_test: The published solution recommends guesses differing in one vowel or consonant, then subtracting known contributions.

suggested_test.description: Choose two candidate distance rules and submit a valid pair of inputs whose predicted output differences disagree.

cards.transfer_when: Known inputs and outputs provide calibration before an unknown target must be recovered.
cards.dont_transfer_when: Several input features change together, or a guessed component is subtracted as if already certain.
cards.outcome_limit: These are published diagnostics, not a recorded history of a solver running them.
cards.lesson: Calibrate on known cases and change one informative component at a time.

cards.source_title: Something Is Off — official solution and author notes
cards.scope_read: Text of all eight PDF pages; solutions and construction notes, without independently resolving the diagrams.
cards.observed: Several clue sets are symmetric although particular required regions or counts cannot be symmetric.
cards.representation_shift: Keep both legal completions instead of importing the usual expectation of uniqueness.
cards.documented_test: The published arguments construct reflected or rotated completions under unchanged clues.

suggested_test.description: Enumerate a small component using explicit rules only; identify any extra convention that removes an otherwise legal completion.

cards.transfer_when: A genre convention conflicts with observable symmetry or an explicit count.
cards.dont_transfer_when: Uniqueness is an explicit requirement, or a second completion violates a stated rule.
cards.outcome_limit: The source intentionally uses two solutions; ambiguity elsewhere does not establish the same intent.
cards.lesson: Treat genre expectations as hypotheses until the artifact supports them.

cards.source_title: Colors — official solution and author notes
cards.scope_read: Complete solution text and construction notes; exact color values supplied by the source.
cards.observed: Hexadecimal color strings form small grids with restricted symbol distributions and replaced characters.
cards.representation_shift: Treat colors as exact encoded characters, then apply the separate structures revealed by those characters.
cards.documented_test: The published solution repairs missing characters using each grid’s internal rules.
cards.documented_false_start: Constructor notes reject a flag-color idea because there was no canonical set of hexadecimal values.

suggested_test.description: Freeze an encoding from one clear group and check whether it explains an untouched group without adjusting measured values.

cards.transfer_when: The artifact exposes reproducible values and several independent anomalies become structured under one encoding.
cards.dont_transfer_when: Only approximate displayed colors are available, or values must be tuned until letters appear.
cards.outcome_limit: The original data contain exact values; the same method is unreliable on altered screenshots.
cards.lesson: Prefer representations that explain several anomalies and depend on reproducible observations.

cards.source_title: Line Plots — official solution and author notes
cards.scope_read: Complete solution text and author notes; graphs not independently reconstructed.
cards.observed: Graphs combine dates, unusual numeric jumps, and icons that recur across series.
cards.representation_shift: Coordinates represent release dates and numbers in titles; icons supply other title components.
cards.documented_test: The author reports that testsolvers used release years and enumerations to identify unfamiliar series.

suggested_test.description: Infer the axes from one recognizable series and predict several points in another before looking up its name.

cards.transfer_when: Dates and discontinuous numbering suggest labels or catalog conventions rather than a measured physical quantity.
cards.dont_transfer_when: The model explains only one graph or requires unconstrained omissions and rescaling.
cards.outcome_limit: The author explicitly documents omitted installments and a subtitle-icon exception.
cards.lesson: Establish what the axes mean before fitting a numerical pattern.

cards.source_title: Cuspidation — official solution and author notes
cards.scope_read: Complete textual mechanism and construction notes; animations not replayed.
cards.observed: Arrowheads, circled letters, intersections, and a timeline appear together.
cards.representation_shift: The picture represents moving arrows; particular collisions remove letters at determined times.
cards.documented_trigger: Constructor account: the initial goal was a new logic puzzle whose rules were conveyed visually.
cards.documented_test: Constructor account: candidate relaunch phrases were simulated to reject head-on collisions.
cards.documented_false_start: An earlier extraction used a separate letter grid; the constructor replaced it with a second launch.

suggested_test.description: Fit launch times to a small collision set and predict an unused intersection, including events that must not occur.

cards.transfer_when: Directional objects and time markers jointly support interpreting a picture as a process.
cards.dont_transfer_when: Motion is only metaphorical, or event timing has no checkable consequences.
cards.outcome_limit: The source explains the finished simulation; no independent replay was performed for this card.
cards.lesson: A dynamic interpretation should predict both events and forbidden events.

cards.source_title: Ministry of Word Searches — official solution and author notes
cards.scope_read: Main solution and author notes through generator reconstruction; appendix not reviewed.
cards.observed: Refreshes change word placements while the same names and fragments of filler recur.
cards.representation_shift: Model identifier-dependent placement cycles, wrapping, and overwrite order instead of treating grids independently.
cards.documented_test: The published method compares consecutive identifiers, beginning with a word that alternates between two positions.

suggested_test.description: Fit the smallest periodic subsystem, freeze its parameters, and predict positions for identifiers not used in fitting.

cards.transfer_when: Repeated instances preserve identities while a small controllable input changes arrangement.
cards.dont_transfer_when: Instances are independently random or the apparent period vanishes on new identifiers.
cards.outcome_limit: The source reconstructs the generator; its large-number computation was not repeated in this audit.
cards.lesson: A simple subsystem can expose a generator that organizes the entire artifact.

cards.source_title: Make Your Own Crossword — official solution and author notes
cards.scope_read: Complete solution text, example input/output grids, and author notes.
cards.observed: A valid submitted grid returns with consistent replacements for its characters.
cards.representation_shift: The crossword is an experimental input that exposes an unknown character mapping.
cards.documented_test: The published example revises its input to include previously absent letters and recover additional mapping entries.

suggested_test.description: List unobserved input categories and design the next valid submission to cover several of them; check repeated characters for consistency.

cards.transfer_when: An interface accepts chosen inputs and returns a stable transformation with observable gaps.
cards.dont_transfer_when: Mappings depend on unmodeled context or submission rules cannot be satisfied by the proposed probe.
cards.outcome_limit: The example improves coverage; it does not establish an optimal query strategy.
cards.lesson: Choose the next input to resolve a named information gap.

cards.source_title: Holistic — official solution and author notes
cards.scope_read: Complete solution text; invariant arguments in questions 4 and 8 inspected, move strings not independently executed.
cards.observed: Several game subquestions ask whether a destination or configuration is attainable.
cards.representation_shift: Track properties preserved or alternated by moves instead of enumerating every move sequence.
cards.documented_test: The published arguments compare checkerboard populations and relate square color to reachable orientations.

suggested_test.description: State a candidate invariant, check every legal move type, then compare the initial state with the proposed target.

cards.transfer_when: A large move space has a small quantity whose update can be proved for every move.
cards.dont_transfer_when: An overlooked move breaks the claimed invariant or an invariant is mistaken for a sufficient condition.
cards.outcome_limit: The invariants address particular subquestions; game identification and extraction remain separate steps.
cards.lesson: Use a short obstruction to prune search while retaining the distinction between necessary and sufficient conditions.

cards.source_title: Beige Flags — official solution
cards.scope_read: Mechanism explanation and solution table; original flag images not independently identified.
cards.observed: City flags are paired with sentences containing enumerated missing phrases.
cards.representation_shift: Compare the identified city with its solved phrase: the phrase uses the same letters plus one additional letter.

suggested_test.description: Solve a clear image and phrase independently, compare their letter counts, then test the unchanged relation on a second pair.

cards.transfer_when: Two independently interpretable channels are paired and their lengths or counts suggest a fixed relation.
cards.dont_transfer_when: One identification is selected only because it yields a desired extra letter.
cards.outcome_limit: The official table supplies consistent pairings but no historical discovery account.
cards.lesson: Let independently obtained identifications constrain one another without hiding uncertainty.

cards.source_title: Writing a solver for Net
cards.scope_read: Complete essay, including local domains, loop avoidance, reachability bounds, and unimplemented parity.
cards.observed: Some connections can be fixed while the orientations of their adjacent tiles remain ambiguous.
cards.representation_shift: Represent tile domains and edge domains separately; add component information and directional reachability bounds.
cards.documented_trigger: Tatham reports noticing deductions that did not require fixing a whole tile.
cards.documented_test: The generalized connectivity rule handles the exceptional two-square board described in the account.
cards.documented_false_start: Tatham initially rotated pieces by trial and error before noticing forced deductions.

suggested_test.description: Find an ambiguous tile with a forced edge; test any generalized connectivity rule on the smallest legal exceptional board.

cards.transfer_when: Relations become certain before the objects containing them, or several local tricks share a boundary condition.
cards.dont_transfer_when: The puzzle permits cycles or disconnected components excluded by Net’s rules.
cards.outcome_limit: This concerns a reusable game, not one instance; regional parity was not implemented in the described solver.
cards.lesson: Store partial certainty and seek one invariant behind special cases.

cards.source_title: How to write a new puzzle
cards.scope_read: Sections 6.1 and 6.2.1 on fairness, observational equivalence, and generation; implementation sections excluded.
cards.observed: The guide distinguishes a reachable solution from one discoverable using available information.
cards.representation_shift: When hidden arrangements cannot be distinguished by any permitted observation, the accepted object can be an equivalence class.

suggested_test.description: Construct two hidden states satisfying every observable constraint and specify whether the task accepts both or requires a distinguishing observation.

cards.transfer_when: A hidden-state puzzle appears ambiguous despite all available observations being exhausted.
cards.dont_transfer_when: The task explicitly demands the original hidden state and actually supplies evidence distinguishing it.
cards.outcome_limit: General construction guidance, not a particular solve trace; acceptance criteria vary by game.
cards.lesson: Separate existence, discoverability, and identifiability before claiming a unique solution.

cards.source_title: Solving bENDs
cards.scope_read: Physical attempt, input model, coordinate representation, pruning, and incomplete-verification sections.
cards.observed: One assembled net yielded words and a single number in each viewing direction.
cards.representation_shift: Encode the net as a parent-linked tree with face centers and orientations.
cards.documented_trigger: The author reports that manipulating small printouts became too frustrating to continue by hand.
cards.documented_test: Fold counts, reused face centers, cube counts, and numbers per viewing direction pruned candidates.
cards.documented_false_start: Representing faces by corner coordinates made transformations cumbersome.

suggested_test.description: Verify closure, exposed faces, and projection independently on a remaining candidate before using readable extraction as confirmation.

cards.transfer_when: A physical manipulation has a compact local transformation but is difficult to perform reliably.
cards.dont_transfer_when: The symbolic model omits collision or visibility constraints that determine physical validity.
cards.outcome_limit: The author explicitly says cube-count filtering admitted invalid foldings; extraction narrowed candidates without full geometric verification.
cards.lesson: A useful representation can accelerate discovery while leaving a clearly stated verification gap.

cards.source_title: Teammate Hunt 2025 Author Notes — Black or White or Moon or Sun
cards.scope_read: Combined-loop puzzle’s high-level and low-level design sections, including its introductory feeder context.
cards.observed: Related small examples and symbol counts help establish a combined loop rule set.
cards.representation_shift: Room types form a bipartite relationship that supports propagation across the grid.
cards.documented_trigger: Chen sought another closed-loop genre that could be combined with Masyu.
cards.documented_test: He alternated automated solution/uniqueness checks with hand solving while changing givens.
cards.documented_false_start: A version without given moons removed the sun-or-moon reasoning he wanted solvers to use.

suggested_test.description: Freeze the inferred rules after a small example and test another grid against both legality and supplied counts.

cards.transfer_when: Repeated examples and redundant totals can confirm a proposed combination of familiar rule systems.
cards.dont_transfer_when: Counts are forced into a checksum interpretation without testing competing roles.
cards.outcome_limit: This documents design choices, not a particular solver’s discovery; automated uniqueness alone did not establish a satisfying solve path.
cards.lesson: Use teaching examples and independent checks to support rule induction.

cards.source_title: Advice To The Puzzlers
cards.scope_read: Believe the testsolvers section; surrounding hunt-management advice excluded.
cards.observed: Berlin warns that author expectations and testsolvers’ actual interpretations often diverge.
cards.representation_shift: Treat intended signaling separately from evidence about what an unspoiled solver notices.

suggested_test.description: Give the artifact to a fresh solver without the favored interpretation and compare which details drive their next action.

cards.transfer_when: A proposed mechanism rests mainly on what the constructor supposedly wanted a detail to mean.
cards.dont_transfer_when: An explicit rule is being ignored merely because another interpretation feels more natural.
cards.outcome_limit: General advice and illustrative failure modes; the passage does not report a specific timed trial.
cards.lesson: A plausible association is a hypothesis about intent, not evidence that the intended connection was found.

cards.source_title: Two hundred puzzles, fifty weeks later — Crossed Out
cards.scope_read: Crossed Out account in group writing sessions; general theme/mechanism discussion also inspected.
cards.observed: The assigned answer’s repeated letter led constructors to objects displaying that letter.
cards.representation_shift: An alphabetic character became an arithmetic operator connecting the pictured objects.
cards.documented_trigger: The group linked repeated Xs to objects containing Xs, then to multiplication.
cards.documented_test: The account says pictures were selected and the puzzle was testsolved that evening.

suggested_test.description: For an association, specify its inputs and executable operation, then test it on a second object without changing the rule.

cards.transfer_when: A distinctive feature has both a literal identity and an operational meaning supported by the artifact.
cards.dont_transfer_when: A theme suggests many associations but none determines a repeatable operation.
cards.outcome_limit: Construction history; no detailed testsolver path or test result is supplied.
cards.lesson: Turn a thematic association into a procedure with checkable inputs and outputs.

cards.source_title: Sudoku as Poetry: A Tag-Fusion Masterpiece — Rubio’s answer
cards.scope_read: Answer’s solving account and author follow-up comments; completed grid not independently verified.
cards.observed: Grid deductions and the incomplete poem leave different unresolved choices.
cards.representation_shift: Treat the grid and text as coupled constraints rather than finishing one before using the other.
cards.documented_trigger: Rubio turned to likely letters and words after ordinary Sudoku deductions stalled.
cards.documented_test: The solver reports alternating linguistic completions with grid deductions.

suggested_test.description: Propagate a proposed word through every affected grid constraint and distinguish a likely completion from a forced one.

cards.transfer_when: Two channels independently constrain shared variables, and progress in either can unlock the other.
cards.dont_transfer_when: Natural language plausibility is treated as a proof of uniqueness.
cards.outcome_limit: The grid alone remained underconstrained; the author clarified spectrum ordering in comments.
cards.lesson: Cross-check independent channels while explicitly preserving residual ambiguity.

cards.source_title: When math and english collide! — quarkle’s answer
cards.scope_read: Accepted answer and visible segmentation discussion.
cards.observed: A numeric string uses only three digits and includes a conspicuous repeated run.
cards.representation_shift: Segment digits into letter indices written in another base.
cards.documented_trigger: The solver explicitly cites the digit restriction; a comment identifies the repeated run as helpful.
cards.documented_test: The proposed conversion reproduces the supplied known word.

suggested_test.description: Enumerate alternative segmentations under the same encoding and determine which additional condition selects the proposed word.

cards.transfer_when: A restricted alphabet and a known example jointly constrain an encoding.
cards.dont_transfer_when: A readable result is accepted without checking alternate segmentation or indexing conventions.
cards.outcome_limit: A commenter supplies a different valid letter sequence; readability alone does not prove uniqueness.
cards.lesson: Use structural restrictions to propose an encoding, then test the ambiguity the encoding leaves.

cards.source_title: Find out the rule, then solve it — Beastly Gerbil’s answer
cards.scope_read: Solver’s rule, arithmetic checks, short solving account, and orientation clarification in comments.
cards.observed: The stated arithmetic rule depends on triangle orientation and red-dot adjacency.
cards.representation_shift: Convert visible groups into arithmetic constraints with explicit eligibility conditions.
cards.documented_test: The solver tried two possible pairs beneath a fixed number and rejected the first.
cards.documented_false_start: The first of those two candidate pairs did not work.

suggested_test.description: Check the rule on every eligible group and explain why visually similar excluded groups do not satisfy its eligibility condition.

cards.transfer_when: One tightly constrained local choice divides the remaining search into a few testable branches.
cards.dont_transfer_when: Group orientation is selected after seeing which numerical relation happens to fit.
cards.outcome_limit: Discussion was needed to clarify orientation; the card does not independently prove the solver’s uniqueness claim.
cards.lesson: Make rule scope explicit before treating a counterexample or successful branch as decisive.

cards.source_title: What goes in the diagonal? — answer and corrections
cards.scope_read: Posted answer and author/commenter corrections; original image constraints not independently recomputed.
cards.observed: Rows and columns constrain entries using different word properties.
cards.representation_shift: A missing word must satisfy its row, its column, and the complete phrase.
cards.documented_test: The posted explanation checks local properties; subsequent discussion checks the full phrase.
cards.documented_false_start: The posted bottom-right entry fit locally but was replaced in discussion to complete the intended phrase.

suggested_test.description: Check every candidate against both local properties before testing the global phrase; retain alternatives that still fit.

cards.transfer_when: Several individually plausible entries must jointly form another constrained object.
cards.dont_transfer_when: The global phrase is used to excuse a failed row or column property.
cards.outcome_limit: The final correction is in comments; no exhaustive uniqueness proof is supplied.
cards.lesson: Local validity may be necessary without being sufficient for the complete extraction.

cards.source_title: 2025 MIT Mystery Hunt — Engagements and other Crimes
cards.scope_read: Invitation-puzzle paragraph; neighboring puzzle comments inspected only to separate their events.
cards.observed: An invitation arrived as a PDF without the usual non-puzzle disclaimer; paired dots were found.
cards.representation_shift: Treat the invitation as an object to manipulate, with dot pairs constraining folds.
cards.documented_trigger: The author says the changed presentation prompted suspicion that the invitation was a puzzle.
cards.documented_test: Several teammates found the dots, determined the folds, folded the artifact, and read its answer.

suggested_test.description: Align a clear dot pair on a copy and predict what another pair or exposed text must do under the same manipulation.

cards.transfer_when: Changes to the medium and repeated alignment marks jointly support physical manipulation.
cards.dont_transfer_when: An ordinary formatting difference is the only clue, or folds are chosen to force desired text.
cards.outcome_limit: A compressed collaborative retrospective; it does not attribute every intermediate insight to an individual.
cards.lesson: Explore the medium’s affordances while keeping reported observations separate from presumed prior work.

cards.source_title: /r/vexillologygreatcirclejerk — official solution and construction notes
cards.scope_read: Text of all three PDF pages, including route instructions and construction notes; maps not independently replotted.
cards.observed: Nine flag mashups pair locations; title and flavor text point toward spherical routes and capitals.
cards.representation_shift: Map each flag pair to a great-circle route between capitals and inspect the resulting small triangular regions.

suggested_test.description: Fix the identified locations, capital coordinates, and route convention before testing whether unused pairs participate in the same geometric pattern.

cards.transfer_when: Paired geographic identities are accompanied by independent clues to a particular route and reference point.
cards.dont_transfer_when: Arbitrary points or map projections are adjusted to manufacture intersections.
cards.outcome_limit: The source describes near-intersections enclosing regions, not exact triple intersections; geometry was not independently reproduced.
cards.lesson: Convert paired identities into a constrained spatial relation, with measurement tolerance stated.

cards.source_title: Mixed Drinks — official solution and construction notes
cards.scope_read: Solution explanation and opening construction notes; grid fills not independently checked.
cards.observed: Two alphabetized clue lists match the capacities of sloping diagonals in chalice-shaped grids.
cards.representation_shift: Use the shape as a crossword constraint; later, colored stem bands specify how selected letters interleave.
cards.documented_test: The published explanation aligns independently clued words by length and requires their shared cells to agree.

suggested_test.description: Place several independently solved words using a fixed diagonal convention, then test all crossings and apply one color-order rule to another chalice.

cards.transfer_when: A distinctive layout matches an independently observed length distribution and repeated colors may encode order.
cards.dont_transfer_when: Words must be altered to fit the shape or the ordering changes separately for each example.
cards.outcome_limit: The source presents a solution, not a solver’s discovery chronology.
cards.lesson: Let layout capacity, crossings, and repeated ordering marks constrain each other.

cards.source_title: Spaghetti Stack — official solution and construction notes
cards.scope_read: Mechanism paragraph and construction notes on both PDF pages; full tree labels not independently solved.
cards.observed: Pictures occupy the leaves of a rooted tree; combined labels can be reparsed into new clues.
cards.representation_shift: A node’s answer becomes input to its parent, so the diagram acts as a repeated clue-evaluation procedure.
cards.documented_trigger: Constructor account: pictures were introduced to give the recursive clueing definite endpoints.
cards.documented_test: Constructor account: a central branch was simplified after repeatedly stumping testsolvers.
cards.documented_false_start: An early direct parsing of the final answer seemed too easy to bypass; a subsequent code-based idea also stalled.

suggested_test.description: Evaluate an unworked internal node from its children using the same boundary-change rule and check its parent without inventing extra letters.

cards.transfer_when: A hierarchy repeatedly combines outputs and supplies recognizable leaf inputs.
cards.dont_transfer_when: Every node requires a different arbitrary wordplay convention or the graph has no justified evaluation order.
cards.outcome_limit: The final clue uses theme in selecting its answer; no independent verification of every branch was performed.
cards.lesson: Test whether a diagram expresses a repeated computation and whether its special endpoints bound that computation.

cards.source_title: Inflation — official solution and construction notes
cards.scope_read: Text of all three PDF pages, including the coin motivation, inserted crossword, bond clues, and construction history.
cards.observed: An unusual crossword shape accompanies a cut-coin reference and a separate unused class of bond clues.
cards.representation_shift: Insert the referenced earlier crossword into the gap; bond entries join inner and outer grids.
cards.documented_trigger: Constructor account: a useful word in the historical crossword suggested the mechanism; the coin reference was added later.
cards.documented_false_start: A different coin-identification prototype reached internal testing but was abandoned as too fiddly.

suggested_test.description: Check the proposed insertion against dimensions, crossings, and every unused bond clue before extracting an answer.

cards.transfer_when: A missing region and an independently identified object support a literal repair with constrained joins.
cards.dont_transfer_when: The resemblance is only thematic or the proposed insert does not satisfy crossing clues.
cards.outcome_limit: The historical coin motivated presentation after the core construction; it was not the reported origin of the mechanism.
cards.lesson: An unused clue category can validate a literal operation suggested by the artifact’s shape.

cards.source_title: Locked Room Murder — official solution and construction notes
cards.scope_read: Timeline introduction, selected testimony rows, contradiction/extraction explanation, and construction opening.
cards.observed: Six testimonies share lighting phases and paragraph structure while describing overlapping events.
cards.representation_shift: Interleave paragraphs in character turn order to reconstruct one evolving state; room visits then place feeder letters.
cards.documented_test: The published reconstruction checks one account against the others and links room-visit counts to answer lengths.

suggested_test.description: Freeze the proposed ordering and predict an unexamined meeting or location; reject it if another testimony makes that event impossible.

cards.transfer_when: Multiple narratives describe shared events and expose recurring order or phase markers.
cards.dont_transfer_when: Accounts have no synchronization evidence or contradictions are removed by inventing unstated events.
cards.outcome_limit: The timeline is only one stage; a separate letter-placement mechanism is required to finish the meta.
cards.lesson: Use shared events to align narratives, then test the alignment against independent constraints.

cards.source_title: Accusation — official solution and construction notes
cards.scope_read: Complete one-page PDF.
cards.observed: The preceding meta answer identifies a literary source; the next prompt asks for a culprit and location with an enumeration.
cards.representation_shift: Rearrange the identified title so its words fill the newly requested semantic roles.
cards.documented_trigger: Constructor account: a testsolver bypassed the intended letter-drop step by guessing the literary reference.
cards.documented_test: The authors split the meta and gated its second part after that testsolve.

suggested_test.description: After identifying the reference, freeze its word inventory and test the required roles and enumeration without adding arbitrary words.

cards.transfer_when: An earlier answer supplies a specific reference and a later prompt constrains its reinterpretation.
cards.dont_transfer_when: A thematic guess predicts the final string but leaves the claimed intermediate mechanism unsupported.
cards.outcome_limit: A shortcut can yield a correct answer; it does not demonstrate execution of the intended previous stage.
cards.lesson: Separate successful answer submission from evidence that a proposed mechanism was actually used.

cards.source_title: Writing a soluble-grid generator for Mines
cards.scope_read: Complete essay on solver-guided perturbation and the final checking pass.
cards.observed: Changing mines to unblock a solver can invalidate earlier deductions.
cards.representation_shift: Treat construction as a fallible proposal process and rerun the solver from the original start on the completed candidate.
cards.documented_test: Tatham reports a final run without perturbations before a generated board is released.

suggested_test.description: After any repair, discard the earlier solving trace and replay the final board with the same starting information; reject it if deduction stalls.

cards.transfer_when: An iterative construction changes facts that earlier reasoning depended on.
cards.dont_transfer_when: The checker shares the generator’s unchecked assumptions or a successful partial trace is treated as final validation.
cards.outcome_limit: A reusable game generator, not one instance; solvability is relative to the implemented deduction system and chosen start.
cards.lesson: Creative generation may fail often if an independent final check reliably rejects bad candidates.

cards.source_title: Writing MIT Mystery Hunt 2023 — The Legend
cards.scope_read: The Legend subsection, including recursive coordinates, timed-out checks, testsolving, and final fill selection.
cards.observed: A self-similar triangular layout needed a custom representation for generation and uniqueness checking.
cards.representation_shift: Encode positions as recursive coordinate tuples so adjacency follows the layout’s hierarchy.
cards.documented_trigger: Irpan reports that an answer length of nine suggested the triangular fractal concept.
cards.documented_test: Editors and testsolvers solved drafts by hand; the final fill was selected because its automated check terminated.
cards.documented_false_start: Early encodings generated a fill but left uniqueness checks unfinished, including an overnight run.

suggested_test.description: Check the coordinate mapping on the smallest recursive levels, then verify that every modeled adjacency matches the physical layout.

cards.transfer_when: A repeated spatial construction has awkward global coordinates but simple recursive structure.
cards.dont_transfer_when: The recursive model omits special boundary adjacencies or a timeout is interpreted as a counterexample.
cards.outcome_limit: The final choice had a completed reported check; other suspected-unique fills remained unverified. No solver was rerun here.
cards.lesson: A representation can simplify exact constraints, but incomplete computation remains inconclusive.
